label: DEEP-RESEARCH TASK: study OPTISIGNS' app library specifically. Use WebSearch + WebFetch o

findings.summary:
OptiSigns markets a "140–160+ app" library that is the centerpiece of its product. Apps live inside the content section (Files/Assets → "App" button opens the app gallery), NOT in the screen/player settings — an important distinction: in OptiSigns an "App" is a saved, configured content Asset (e.g., "Lobby Instagram Wall") that then goes into playlists/schedules, whereas raw uploads (image/video/PDF) and web-URLs are the other asset types. The gallery is a paginated grid (~10 pages) with a search box, 9 category filter tabs (All, Misc, News, Finance, Social Media, Photos & Video, File Management, Communication, Business), and per-app plan badges ("Included in all plans", "Standard plan and up", "Pro Plus plan and up") that gate access. Marquee/marketed apps are Instagram, YouTube, Weather, Canva, Facebook, Google Slides, Power BI, Google Reviews, RSS, plus the "Designer" (their built-in Canva-style editor) and OptiSync (their live-data mapping engine). The honest 2026 embed reality is the important finding: the social apps that look "free" mostly now require OAuth to a Business/Creator account (Instagram Graph API via "Sign in with Instagram"; Facebook Page token) or route through paid third-party aggregators (Walls.io, Social Mix) because the public scrape/embed era is over — X/Twitter especially is paywalled and TikTok has no first-class app, only aggregator paths. VenueOS already has widgets (WEBPAGE, SOCIAL_FEED, RSS_FEED, STREAMING, LIVE_DATA, WEATHER, CALENDAR, CHART) that can back most of these apps with an S-effort config-form-over-existing-widget approach; the L-effort items are the OAuth-token integrations (Instagram, Facebook, Google Workspace, Power BI, Microsoft calendar) and anything depending on a paid aggregator.</summary>

<uxNotes>[
"Apps live in the CONTENT layer, not screen settings: operator goes Files/Assets → clicks the 'App' button → the app gallery opens. An 'App' becomes a saved, named, configured Asset (e.g. 'Lobby Instagram Wall') that is then added to playlists and schedules — exactly like an image or video. This is the key conceptual move: an App is a reusable content object, not a per-screen toggle.",
"The gallery is a paginated grid (~10 pages of tiles). Each tile = app icon + name + one-line benefit description (e.g. Instagram: 'Highlight your company's Instagram feed to boost engagement').",
"Top of the gallery has a SEARCH box plus category filter tabs: All, Misc, News, Finance, Social Media, Photos & Video, File Management, Communication, Business (9 tabs). Taxonomy is a bit loose (Weather sits under 'News'; Canva under 'Misc').",
"Per-app PLAN BADGES gate access and upsell: 'Included in all plans', 'Standard plan and up', 'Pro Plus plan and up'. This turns the library into a pricing-tier merchandiser — premium apps (Power BI, Tableau) visibly require the higher tier.",
"Per-app config is a focused form, not a raw URL box. Instagram's form: Name (internal), Display Mode (Single Post / Social Wall / Social Kiosk / Bricks), Theme (Light/Dark/Custom bg), Scroll Speed, Font Size, moderation ('always show new posts'), time/count post filters, QR-code option. Every app has a tailored field set — this is the whole value vs 'paste a URL'.",
"OAuth is inline: social/Google/Microsoft apps show a 'Sign in with Instagram' / 'Sign in with Google' button right in the config, then reveal the rest of the form once connected.",
"Preview without commit: from Screen Management → Edit → 'Preview' the operator sees the configured content on the chosen screen without saving. Plus a 'Virtual Screen' app gives a shareable preview URL for remote staff.",
"App vs Widget vs Asset distinction: OptiSigns markets everything as 'Apps' (140–160+), but under the hood they split into (a) EMBED apps = a configured iframe/feed (YouTube, Website, Slides), (b) DATA apps = API-pulled live data (Weather, Stocks, Reviews, OptiSync-mapped), (c) BUILT-IN content apps = generated on their side (Clock, Countdown, QR, News, Designer), and (d) LAYOUT apps (Split Screen). They deliberately don't expose this taxonomy to the user — it's all just 'Apps'.",
"OptiSync is the sleverage layer: rather than one-off apps, it lets an operator map ANY data source (Google Sheets, Excel, API, DB) onto template fields, powering birthdays, schedules, menus, order-tracking. It reframes 'apps' from 'iframes' to 'live-data-driven templates'.",
"Branded skins over generic engines: CNN/CBC/TechCrunch 'News' apps are the same RSS/news engine with a logo — a cheap way to inflate the app count and give operators recognizable one-click choices."
]</uxNotes>
